title: One of the big wheat sellers cannot ship for a while
plain_question: If a country that supplies a lot of the world's wheat stopped shipping for part of a year, which buyers would have the most to replace, and how much room would they have to do it?
what_this_is: Arithmetic on assumptions you can change, using real trade and stock figures. It is not a forecast, and it does not say this will happen.
what_this_is_not: It does not predict prices, hunger or shortages. It works out how much wheat a country would have to find somewhere else, and shows what it has to fall back on. What would actually happen depends on decisions nobody has made yet.

inputs.label: How much of that supplier's shipments stop
inputs.note: A round starting number, not an estimate of any real event.

inputs.label: How much of the gap can be bought elsewhere
inputs.note: Depends on whether other sellers have spare wheat, whether the buyer can pay for it, and whether it can be shipped in time. Treat this as the question the test is really asking.

displacement.explain: If this country goes looking for wheat from another seller, it will be bidding against whoever else buys from that seller. The countries below depend on the same supplier. The ones with thin stocks and little room in the household budget are the ones a bidding contest would hurt most.
